sense.text:
“I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The children of Israel were to be scattered into corners, and scattered as slaves. That is what happened to the so-called blacks and Hispanics, enslaved and scattered throughout the four corners of the earth. This is talking about us.

The remembrance that we are the children of Israel has ceased from among men. Ask any nation or any man who the children of Israel are, and they will not point to the so-called blacks, Hispanics and North American Indians. Nobody knows any more that we are Israel; that truth is only now starting to come out. After three days and a half the spirit of life from God enters into them and they stand upon their feet, and that is what is taking place right now: the spirit of life from God has entered into us, and we are waking up to the truth hidden from us for centuries.

We are not Americans, not Afro-Americans, not North American Indians. We are not Puerto Ricans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Trinidadians, Ethiopians or South Africans. We are the children of Israel, that is who we be, and we have to make it known.

precepts.why:
Scattered to the four corners of the earth in slavery, Israel would “grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”. Noonday is when the sun is bright in the sky, yet we grope like someone blind trying to find his way: groping in different religions, groping in politics, trying to find out who we are. As a nation of people we do not know who we are. The furthest we can go back is slavery in Africa, but it goes much further than that, so we grope in all these religions and all these names put upon us.

“And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore.” In the places where we were scattered as slaves we will always be oppressed. The oppression here in America is not going to stop, and the oppression our people face all over the world is not going to stop. Many voted for Trump thinking he would make the oppression stop; the rude awakening is that Trump is about to turn up oppression upon our people. That is the prophecy: God says we will always be oppressed and spoiled in the corners where we were scattered as slaves.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”. In the lands where we were scattered as slaves we would serve our enemies. Black man, the white man that enslaved you, that you have been serving for over four hundred years, God calls your enemy. The Arabs that enslaved you, God calls your enemy. Many think the people that enslaved them are their friends; God said no, they are your enemies, and that is who you have been serving.

In the sixties and seventies, in the civil rights movement, you knew who your enemy was: he had the dog on you, he beat you and hosed you down, you could not use the same toilet, drink from the same water fountain or sit on the same seat on the bus. These last decades civil rights made our people forget who their enemy is. The Lord is going to turn that affliction back up on our people so we remember who our enemies are. That is why Trump is in office: the benefits from the US government that made you forget who your enemies are will be taken away.

“Which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. In want of all things: your enemies teach you religion and teach you about God. Black man, you learned your religion, Christianity, from your enemy. You learned your education from your enemy, and your enemy told you who you are: African American, Ghanaian, Kenyan, Ethiopian, Jamaican, Puerto Rican. Everything we know today was told to us by our enemies in slavery. He told you your God is white and looks like him.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The yoke of iron is slavery, and it stayed on our necks until we were destroyed. So when they claim they released us from slavery and the yokes came off our necks, it means we were destroyed. We are a destroyed people, the only people on the earth that do not know who they are or their heritage. The Chinese can look up their ancestry and have their culture; the culture blacks, Hispanics and West Indians follow today was made up on this side of the world in the last fifty or sixty years.

sense.text:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”: into Egypt a second time, but this time with ships. That is the transatlantic slave trade. Israel never went into ancient Egypt again with ships; the Egypt here is America and the lands where we were brought as slaves. This is the last curse written in Deuteronomy 28. The meaning of Egypt is bondage, oppression, to be kept in affliction. Were we not afflicted and oppressed here in America, enslaved and in bondage here in America? This is the last captivity we would go into.

“By the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: the Egypt Israel had just been delivered from, ancient Egypt, they would see no more. So the Egypt we were to go back into in slavery on ships is a new Egypt, and that Egypt is America and all these lands, mainly America.

“And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”. Where the slave ships took us, there we were sold to our enemies: on the shores of Virginia in America, of Haiti, of Jamaica, in England and Britain. By Bible prophecy the Israelites would be sold as slave men and slave women to their enemies, and that prophecy fits the children of the transatlantic slave trade. The so-called white man that calls himself a Jew today was never sold on ships to his enemies for slave men and slave women. That does not fit them. They are not the people of God; they are not the Jews according to the Bible.

“And no man shall buy you.” Dumb Christians and their translations twist this, saying we sold ourselves and nobody bought us back, or that we offered ourselves as slaves and were refused. That makes no damn sense; it never happened to anybody in history. When you look at these commentaries you take the meat and throw away the bone. The same word is used by Nehemiah, and there it is translated redeem. So no man shall buy you means no man shall redeem you, no man shall free you: nobody would be able to purchase us back. When we were stolen as slaves to this side of the earth, nobody came with money to buy us or redeem us, none of our brothers and none of our leaders. But Christ came and died, and with his blood he paid that price for us.

precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. The dead bodies are the Israelites: our dead bodies lie in the street of the great city. That place is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. It is not literal Egypt but spiritual Egypt.

So when Deuteronomy 28:68 says the Lord shall bring us into Egypt again with ships, it is talking about the future, about a spiritual Egypt. That is why it is the last curse: we would go into slavery on ships, and it happened to us, our people, the children of Israel.

“And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.” When we came out of Egypt, we never went back into Egypt again as slaves as a nation of people.

So when Moses says in Deuteronomy 28:68, “by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”, he is letting us know the Egypt he is talking about is not the ancient Egypt we had just been delivered from. It is not ancient Egypt we would go back into as slaves on ships. It is a new Egypt, America and the lands where we were made slaves.

“And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen”. The same word that is translated buy in Deuteronomy 28:68 is used here by Nehemiah, and here it is translated redeemed. Nehemiah and them went and paid money and bought back their brothers that were sold to the heathens. They redeemed them; they paid money and got them back.

So in Deuteronomy 28:68, when we are sold unto our enemies “and no man shall buy you”, it means nobody would be able to purchase us back or redeem us. You can’t fool us; we understand the Bible.

Nehemiah keeps on: “and will ye even sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their peace”.

“And whosoever lieth carnally with a woman, that is a bondmaid, betrothed to an husband, and not at all redeemed”. A bondmaid is a servant, a slave, and not at all redeemed means nobody paid money to buy her back; nobody bought her. Then “nor freedom given her”: to redeem goes into freedom given.

So when Nehemiah went and redeemed, or bought, our brothers, he really freed them from slavery. And in Deuteronomy 28:68, no man shall buy thee means nobody will free you from that slavery and that captivity. It is the same word: no man shall redeem thee, no man shall free thee.

“She shall be scourged; they shall not be put to death, because she was not free.”

“Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen.” That happened to the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered among the heathen on cargo slave ships.

“Thou sellest thy people for nought”: God sold his people and got nothing in return when he allowed the nations to enslave us and scatter us in slavery, “and dost not increase thy wealth by their price.” God did not get rich off of us when we were sold as slaves; the white man got rich off of us.

“Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.” We are made a reproach unto the nations; they scorn us and hold us in derision. “Thou makest us a byword among the heathen”: they call us all types of names, lazy, no good, violent, look at how they live. “A shaking of the head among the people”: when the people see us, they shake their heads. “My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me”.

“Thus saith the Lord, Where is the bill of your mother’s divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you?” We were sold into slavery, and the mother is Israel, the land, put away. “Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away.”

For our iniquities we sold ourselves. In Deuteronomy 28 God says if you keep these commandments the blessings will come upon you; if you don’t keep the commandments the curses will come upon you, you will go into slavery on ships and be scattered throughout the four corners of the earth. We broke God’s commandments and so we ended up selling ourselves: the Lord allowed our enemies to come and enslave us.

“Wherefore, when I came, was there no man? when I called, was there none to answer?” Nobody answered when God called. “Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver?” The Most High sold us into slavery, but he also said he is going to redeem us: to free us, to save us, to buy us back and pay that price. Deuteronomy 28:68 said no man shall buy you, but God’s hand is not short that he cannot redeem.

sense.text:
“Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy”. The strangers are the other nations that were among Israel, the strangers that came out of Egypt amongst us. God says we could buy them and use them as servants: “they shall be your possession”, and “they shall be your bondmen for ever.” That will be in force again when Christ returns.

“But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” We are not supposed to enslave our own people and rule over our own people with rigour. In the past we did it: tribes fought with each other and enslaved each other, and that literally happened among the twelve tribes of Israel. God says do it to the nations, do it to the strangers, but don’t deal like that with your brother.

“And if a sojourner or stranger wax rich by thee, and thy brother that dwelleth by him wax poor, and sell himself unto the stranger”. To sell yourself unto the stranger is to become that person’s servant. Your brother is poor, he has no food and no house, and the stranger is rich, so the brother says, I am going to go serve this stranger, work in his vineyard, work in his field, become a servant for him.

“After that he is sold he may be redeemed again; one of his brethren may redeem him”. To redeem him is to buy him back, to pay money to free him: “his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family may redeem him; or if he be able, he may redeem himself”, paying money for his own freedom.

“And he shall reckon with him that bought him from the year that he was sold to him unto the year of jubile”. The year of jubile is every seven years. To reckon with him is to go to the one that bought him: you paid ten thousand dollars for me, I haven’t worked it off yet, but I have the money right here to pay you. Or his uncle or his brother goes and says, our nephew sold himself to you for ten thousand dollars, we will pay it, let him go free.

“And the price of his sale shall be according unto the number of years”. If he was to work ten years and has already done five, and he was bought for thirty grand, you don’t pay the same thirty grand; he already did half the time, so you pay half the money to free him from the bondage he put on himself. That is “the price of his redemption out of the money that he was bought for”: that is how a brother, an uncle or a family member that sold himself as a servant is redeemed.

“And as a yearly hired servant shall he be with him”: like the jobs people do today, hired as a servant for a year. “And the other shall not rule with rigour over him in thy sight.” This is how Israel should deal with each other. Even today, in Haiti and in Trinidad, people with nowhere to stay become servants: Venezuela is messed up, many Venezuelans have moved to Trinidad, and they give their kids over to clean house and cook, saying I will work for you, just give me somewhere to stay and pay me. That is what this is going into.

“And if he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he, and his children with him.” You have to let him go, and that lets you know even the stranger read about here is talking about Israel. The year of jubile is the year of redemption.

“For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt”. We are servants to God, not to any man.

All of this is what Deuteronomy 28:68 is going into when it says no man shall buy you: nobody would go pay money to redeem us or get us out of slavery. When we were stolen as slaves to this side of the earth, nobody came with money to buy us, redeem us or give us freedom, the way Nehemiah redeemed his brothers that were sold as slaves. Nobody was able to do that when we were brought here on cargo slave ships to serve that hard bondage in America and throughout the Caribbean islands.

precepts.why:
Some might say making the nations bondmen is not Godlike or Christlike, so go to the prophecy. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. In the future God will have mercy upon us, choose us, the Israelites, and put us back in our land. “And the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”.

“And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”. The house of Israel, the twelve tribes, you so-called blacks and Hispanics, will possess the nations, the strangers, for servants and handmaids: the same thing read in Leviticus 25.

“And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were”. We were captives in all these lands, America, Europe, Arabia, and the Bible says we will take them captives whose captives we were.

Some still say Christ isn’t doing that when he returns, so read what Christ said: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”. If you overcome your sins and the tribulations and trials you go through on this earth, and keep the commandments, you will have power over the nations, the nations as slaves, you ruling over them. That is what the kingdom of heaven is about.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”. They are not ruling with you; you rule them, with a rod of iron, meaning you are not going to play with them.

“If any man have an ear, let him hear.” This is the prophecy, the judgment written for the nations that enslaved us and brought us over here on cargo slave ships. God is a just God. You are not going to enslave God’s people, lynch us and oppress us, and say that was in the past, it wasn’t me. There is judgment written for what your fathers did.

“He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity”, by the children of Israel. Those that led the children of Israel into slavery are going into slavery, as read in Isaiah 14, and the law of Leviticus 25 will be in force again when Christ returns.

sense.text:
The Most High said his hand is not short that he cannot save us and redeem us. “Shake thyself from the dust”: in these lands we have been under the dust, laid down on the floor with the nations walking upon us, and God says shake yourself from it. “Arise”: wake up to who you are; you are the sons of God. “And sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck”. The bands of our neck are this captivity, and the lies and philosophies we learned here in slavery.

“O captive daughter of Zion”: the daughters of Zion are captives in the different lands we were scattered to as slaves. Some of you don’t have the yoke on your neck, but you are still captive. Some think they are free; no, we are still captives, in the land of our captivity.

“For thus saith the Lord, Ye have sold yourselves for nought”. We sold ourselves for nought by worshipping idols, going after other gods. We allowed ourselves to be sold: because we worshipped idols and went against our God, these curses came upon us and we were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth as slaves.

“And ye shall be redeemed without money.” To redeem is to free, to buy. The Lord is going to make a purchase and buy us back, but he is not going to use money to redeem us. Under the law every firstborn needed money to be redeemed, and Judas Maccabeus sent silver up to Jerusalem for his slain brothers, but we are redeemed, bought and freed without money. No man could buy us; Christ bought us, and the price is his blood.

precepts.why:
“As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world”. An idol is nothing.

So when Isaiah 52:3 says “Ye have sold yourselves for nought”, it means we sold ourselves for idols. By worshipping idols and going after other gods we allowed ourselves to be sold, and the curses came upon us.

To show what being redeemed with money is: “Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall be mine: I am the Lord.” The Levites belong to the Lord. For the firstborn over and above the number of the Levites, “Thou shalt even take five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary”, “And thou shalt give the money, wherewith the odd number of them is to be redeemed, unto Aaron and to his sons.”

You had to give money to be redeemed. Every firstborn brought into this world had to pay money to be redeemed according to the law. “And Moses took the redemption money”, “And Moses gave the money of them that were redeemed unto Aaron and to his sons, according to the word of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.” This was the law kept concerning every firstborn in Israel: that soul had to be redeemed with money.

There is a reason the firstborn had to be redeemed with money, and the Lord says the firstborn belongs to him, but that is for another time.

“Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, which they bring unto the Lord, whether it be of men or beasts, shall be thine”. The matrix is the woman’s womb, the portal into this world. “Nevertheless the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem. And those that are to be redeemed from a month old shalt thou redeem, according to thine estimation, for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.”

These things are a shadow of things to come. For every firstborn a price, money, had to be paid for that soul to be redeemed, and all of that goes into something spiritual: the firstborn, the firstfruits, the best of the best, the firstborn of many brethren. Under the law you had to pay money to be redeemed or purchased unto the Lord. That is why it stands out that Isaiah says we are redeemed without money.

See what Judas Maccabeus did. Judas called upon the Lord to be their helper and leader of the battle, and rushing upon Gorgias’ men, “he put them to flight.” “And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.” The day following they came to take up the bodies of their brothers that were slain, “and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.”

“Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.” These brothers had idols under their clothing, and that is why the Lord allowed them to die in that battle. Judas and his men prayed for them, “that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance”, and Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin.

“And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering”, “in that he was mindful of the resurrection”. Judas Maccabeus and our forefathers understood the resurrection: “For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead.” “Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.”

He made that reconciliation by sending the money up. By the law, he tried to redeem those brothers with money: the same money paid for every firstborn to redeem their soul. But Israel shall be redeemed without money.

We shall be redeemed, brought back and freed without money. “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price”.

We are not our own; we are bought. When Deuteronomy 28:68 says no man shall buy you, none of our brothers or our leaders was able to buy us or free us from captivity and oppression, or redeem us. But Christ came and died and paid that price for us. Christ is the one that bought us; he redeemed us and bought us with a price.

What is that price? “And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.”

Thirty pieces of silver is what they paid to kill Christ, our King. That was his price, what they gave his brother Judas to deliver him up to be killed.

“And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.” Those thirty pieces of silver were the price of Christ’s blood.

So when it says we are bought with a price, the price is the blood of Christ. That is the payment for us to be let go from slavery, the payment for our freedom: his blood is what he used to buy us back. No man was able to buy us or free us, but with his blood Christ paid the price to redeem us.

“Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold”. We were not bought, purchased or freed with corruptible things. We sold ourselves for nought and shall be redeemed without money. Silver and gold is what was read in the Old Testament: every firstborn that came out of the matrix had to be redeemed with money, and Judas Maccabeus sent shekels up to Jerusalem and prayed for the brothers that died in sin.

“From your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers”. The tradition of the fathers is what was read in Leviticus and Numbers: the shekels, the money paid to the priest in the temple to redeem every firstborn. We were not redeemed with those things.

“But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”. That is how we are freed, how we were bought: the price we were bought with is Christ’s blood. He is that lamb without blemish and without spot, meaning he walked perfect on this earth, without sin, and we are redeemed through his blood. No man would be able to save us, redeem us or free us, but Christ purchased us with his blood.

sense.text:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law”: Christ bought us, Christ freed us. The curse of the law is in Deuteronomy 28, and one of those curses is going into slavery again with ships and being sold unto our enemies, with no man to buy us. Christ has redeemed us from slavery; the curse of the law is slavery.

“Being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. He was made a curse for us when he was murdered, crucified: they hanged him on a tree and killed him. In his dying, his blood redeemed us. That was the price paid for us to be redeemed and freed. The Lord said we sold ourselves for nought and would be redeemed without money, and we were redeemed with Christ’s blood, not with shekels, silver and gold.

precepts.why:
What is the curse of the law Christ redeemed us from? “But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

And among those curses, verse 68: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. That is us going into slavery again, back into oppression and affliction, into countries that afflict us, on cargo slave ships. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” No man would redeem us, no man would pay that price or that money to get us back. But Christ came and died and paid the ultimate price, his blood, to redeem us and free us.

“Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity”. Christ gave himself for us, and the us is the Israelites, the twelve tribes of Israel. We broke God’s commandments, the curses came upon us and we were scattered in slavery, so Christ came and died and redeemed us with his blood, so we could be let go out of slavery. He purchased us with his blood; now we belong to him.

“And purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.” That peculiar people is us, zealous of good works when we keep the commandments. “These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority.”

“But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law”. God sent forth Christ, made of a woman: he came just the way we came. Made under the law: circumcised on the eighth day, keeping the passover, the dedication and all the feast days.

“To redeem them that were under the law”. This shows who redemption is for, and this is for you dumb Christians: it is for those that were under the law. Were all nations under the law? No. Were the Chinese under the law? Was Esau under the law? Never. Christ came and died for those under the law because they broke the law, the curses came upon them, they sold themselves for nought and were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth in slavery. So Christ died and paid that price to get them out, to redeem us from under the curse of the law, which is slavery.

“That we might receive the adoption of sons”: so that now we might be the sons of God.

After Christ died and rose, “Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.” He changed his appearance so they could not tell it was him; Christ was messing with them. “What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?”

Cleopas answered, “Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem”, which also shows who the strangers are: foreigners. They told him, “Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people: And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him.”

“But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel”. Redeem who? Israel. That is not rocket science, and that is after he died. Christ redeemed Israel: he paid that price for Israel to be redeemed from under the curses, and he is the one that bought us with his blood to let us go out of slavery.

“Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.” The Lord scattered us because we broke his commandments: he allowed our enemies to come against us and scatter us into slavery. And God is going to gather us back and keep us as a shepherd does his flock.

“For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him”. The Lord redeemed us by coming and dying and paying that price for us, and that Lord is Christ. To ransom something is to give something in return for something. What the Lord gave in return for Jacob to redeem him was his blood, his life: our King gave his life to redeem us. We sold ourselves for nought and were redeemed without money; it was not money used to purchase us but the blood of Christ. That was the ransom.

“From the hand of him that was stronger than he”: the nations, those afflicting us.

“And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood”. Christ was slain and has redeemed us, Israel, to God, by his blood. We are purchased with the blood of Christ, redeemed by Christ’s blood.

“Out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation”: because Israel was enslaved and scattered among all people, tongues and nations. The Lord paid that price for us to be freed from these lands where we were made slaves.

sense.text:
“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel”. The Lord God of who? Israel. Christians read this and still don’t get it; they say he is the God of all nations. This is easy reading comprehension.

“For he hath visited and redeemed his people”. His people are the children of the slave trade. He had to redeem them because they were scattered into slavery on cargo slave ships, and it says no man shall buy them. But our King, our God, paid that price and bought us out of captivity; in his dying he freed us out of captivity.

When did the Lord God of Israel visit and redeem his people? He visited us means he literally came on the earth: the God of Israel came in the flesh, visited us and redeemed us with his blood by dying for us. He paid that price to get us from under the curse: from slavery, from captivity, from oppression, from the curse of the law.

“And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began”. Ever since the world began, the prophets have been talking about Christ.

“That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is why Christ came and died: to save us from our enemies. We were enslaved and scattered throughout the four corners of the earth among our enemies, living in the land of our enemies, oppressed by our enemies. Our God came and died to deliver us from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us.

precepts.why:
Who is the Lord God of Israel that visited and redeemed his people? “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him”. “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” When did the God that created Israel show himself on the earth and converse with men? That is Luke 1:68: the Lord God of Israel visited and redeemed his people. We all know who redeemed us, and what he used to redeem us.

“He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.” This is what Baruch said: he showed himself on the earth and conversed with men. He created the world and all of us; this is Christ, Yahawashi. He created the world, created Israel, created this earth, and he came into the world and the world did not know him as the God that created everything, the Son of God that created everything.

“And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us”. Baruch said he would come on the earth and converse with men, and here the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.

“And we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father”. The only begotten is the only son God created, which is Christ, which is a God, and he created everything else. “Full of grace and truth.”

“And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness”. A controversy is arguments and contentions: we are not arguing or contending with anybody about the divinity of Christ. You read in the scripture that he created all things and then turn around and say Christ is not a God? It is a mystery, going into Christ and his Father, so not everybody will get it. The elect will. The Lord reveals his secrets unto his servants the prophets.

“God was manifest in the flesh”: that is what was read in Baruch 3, in John 1, and in Luke 1:68, the Lord God of Israel visiting and redeeming his people. “Justified in the Spirit”: the God justified in the spirit is Christ. “Seen of angels”: the angels are the apostles, the leaders, who saw him. “Preached unto the Gentiles”: Christ was taught unto the Gentiles. “Believed on in the world”: thousands followed after him through the apostles. “Received up into glory”: the God made flesh was received up into glory, sitting on the right hand side of his Father.

What does it mean that he visited his people? “Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.”

That is our God on the earth, literally with us: our God made flesh and dwelling with us.

“Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel, and his redeemer the Lord of hosts”. Who is his Redeemer? The Lord of hosts. This is talking about the Father too, but it is talking about Christ: he is the Redeemer, the Lord of hosts, and Christ is speaking on behalf of the Father here.

“I am the first, and I am the last”. It is not a coincidence that he keeps saying I am. Who is the I am, the first and the last? This is the Lord of hosts speaking.

“And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.” Christ is speaking here, and his reward is eternal life and rulership of this earth.

“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.” That is what was just read in Isaiah 44:6: the Redeemer, the Lord of hosts, who says I am the first and I am the last, is Christ. He is the I am read about all through the scriptures. Those that get it get it; for those that don’t, it wasn’t meant for them to get it.

Isaiah 54 opens with the barren that did not bear, and more are the children of the desolate than of the married wife: that is us in the future, Jerusalem full of us, the innumerable multitude going back into our own land. “Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded; for thou shalt not be put to shame: for thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more.” We will not be ashamed or confused, and we will forget all the shame we went through.

“For thy Maker is thine husband; the Lord of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel”. Who is the Maker, the Lord of hosts, the Redeemer? The Holy One of Israel, as in Isaiah 45: the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker.

“The God of the whole earth shall he be called.” Who is the God of the whole earth? Christ is the God of the whole earth. He is our Redeemer.

This explains the hand of all that hate us: “And he saved them from the hand of him that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.”

The Lord saves us from the hand of them that hate us, from the hand of our enemies. He redeemed us: he paid that price, he bought us with a price, he freed us. The enemy Christ came to redeem us from is the same thing read in Luke 1:71: him redeeming us is saving us from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters that are afraid, going through oppression, and in the future when Esau turns it up on us, putting us in prison and killing us: be strong, don’t give up the fight in this war, don’t be afraid.

“Behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence”. Who is our God that comes with vengeance? Christ, and Christ is called God. He is going to pay back the nations for what they have done to us. “He will come and save you.”

“For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper.” The Lord will deliver us when we cry out to him. “He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy. He shall redeem their soul from deceit and violence”. Violence is coming to us here in the streets of Babylon, but the Lord is going to redeem us and deliver us from it.

“And precious shall their blood be in his sight.” Some of us are going to die here in Babylon doing the work of our God, but God says don’t worry, your blood is precious in his sight.

“For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”. That speaks of when Christ returns in the end, but it also goes into when he came on the earth, redeemed us and gave his life for us: that is Emmanuel, our God with us.

“And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”. Even though the worms destroy his body and he dies, in his flesh he will see God: “Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”. With his own eyes he will see Christ, which is his God. Job is a mighty prophet: he was here when his Redeemer came and died for his sins, the Lord is also going to resurrect him, and he is here again today.

“Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro?” This is Zion, the land, speaking. All of us were scattered in slavery throughout the four corners of the earth, and the land is desolate: the children of Israel are not dwelling in it, occupying it or ruling it today. We were captive, moved to and fro. “Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?” These are the elect, the innumerable multitude.

“And they shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers”: they will be our servants, us taking them captives whose captives we were. “They shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet”, in the kingdom, when we are set back up to rule this earth. Some brothers have white people bowing down to them in videos while they are still in slavery, still oppressed by the white man; they have their reward. The glory is when kings bow down to you, not some regular Edomite but kings, nobles and presidents. “For they shall not be ashamed that wait for me”: those of us that wait on the Lord our Redeemer.

“Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered?” We are the prey, and the mighty is America, Europe, the lands where we were made slaves. The Lord has redeemed us and is going to take us out of these lands: “the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” The terrible is the nations that made war with us and enslaved us; the Lord is going to fight them.

“And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine”: all the nations that oppress us will be cannibals eating their own flesh. “And all flesh shall know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer”. That Lord is Christ, our Saviour and our Redeemer.

sense.text:
Many times in the Old Testament the Lord and God are talking about Christ, and sometimes about his Father. Christ has authority over everything: he created everything, all things were created by him and for him, and if you created everything by you and for you, that makes you a God. “The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”.

But Christ is not the Ancient of days. Christ has a Father that created him, and Christ created us and the whole earth: the Father told him what to do and he did it. Christianity says the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are all one; that is bull crap.

“The Lord is a man of war”. Who is this Lord that is a man of war? Solomon explained what Moses was talking about: it is the Word of God, the Almighty Word, that leaped down from his royal throne as a fierce man of war. Christ has a throne, and his Father has a throne.

precepts.why:
“For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course”: everybody was sleeping. This is when the Lord came down and killed all the firstborn in Egypt. “Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war”.

The Almighty Word is the Word of God, Christ. So when Exodus 15 says the Lord is a man of war, it is talking about the Word of God that leaped down from the throne as a man of war. Christ has a throne; Christ is sitting on a throne.

“While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.” Christ “had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him”: our people did not believe, “That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled”. “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted”, converted by Christ.

“These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him.” Isaiah saw the glory of Christ and spoke of Christ. That is not hard reading comprehension. And the same way Isaiah prophesied the eyes of the Pharisees would be blinded, today many of our people’s eyes are going to be blinded to what is brought out here.

“In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” The Lord here is Christ, the Word of God read in Wisdom of Solomon that leaped off his royal throne and came down as a man of war. This is his throne.

“Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.” The Lord of hosts here is Christ. Then Isaiah said, “Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.”

That is when John says Isaiah saw his glory and spoke of him. The King, the Lord of hosts, is the Word of God, Christ on his throne. And the Father has a throne too.

“The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The first man, Adam, is of the earth; Christ is the Lord from heaven, the Lord Isaiah saw sitting on his throne in Isaiah 6, the King.

Revelation says the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it. That is two thrones.

Daniel saw the throne of God. “I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: all the kingdoms and rulership on this earth cast down. “And the Ancient of days did sit”. The Ancient of days was before days began, with no beginning of days and no end of days, so this is the Father, Christ’s Father, Yahawashi’s Father. This is in the future, after Christ brings everything into subjection and gives it all up, all of us and this whole earth, to the Father.

“Whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.” His wheels are his chariots. That is the throne of the Father. Isaiah 6 is Christ’s throne, and the throne the Almighty Word leaped off in Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 is that throne.

“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.” Christ says if you overcome your sins you will sit with him in his throne. That is why Paul said he would rather die and be with Christ.

Christ came and walked perfectly, and he has access to his Father’s throne. If we overcome, we will sit in Christ’s throne. Christ has a throne and the Father has a throne, and in Revelation 22 the Father’s throne and Christ’s throne are both there.

“Thus saith the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker”. The Holy One of Israel has a Maker that created him. He created us; he is our God, and the adoption of sons is where we become the sons of his God. “Ask me of things to come concerning my sons”: Christ calls us his sons, because he created us.

Christ is speaking on behalf of the Father here, because everything he did, the Father told him to do. And Christ says, “I have made the earth, and created man upon it: I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens, and all their host have I commanded.” “I have raised him up in righteousness”.

“But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever”. This is the Father speaking to the Son, and he calls the Son God. “A sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.”

Therefore God is the Son; even thy God is the Father. The Son and the Father: the Son is called God because he created all of us under the orders of his Father. He is anointed above his fellows, above everything that was created, above all the angels. That is why John says he is preferred before me.

This is where Paul got it from. “Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre.” That God is Yahawashi, the Christ, the Word of God.

“Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” Therefore God is Christ; thy God is his Father, that created him and him alone.
